question: Will the official result of the Lamag by-election (Sabah), scheduled for January 24, 2026, be overturned before May 1, 2026?
summary: Ensemble aggregate is modest at 4%, but objections identify a non-zero risk channel via election petitions in Sabah.
A petition path is credibly possible, though historically overturns are rare and margins here are large, suggesting the base risk is still low.
Threshold analysis indicates overturns by May 1, 2026 are unlikely, given the large Lamag margin and lack of reported reversals to date.
Overall, the calibrated probability remains modestly above the ensemble due to non-zero petition risk and Sabah-specific dynamics.

justification.critique_assessment: Objections are valid in highlighting a non-zero petition route and Sabah-specific dynamics, but the historical rarity of overturns and the large by-election margin argue against a high likelihood of reversal.
justification.adjustment: Adjusted upward from 0.04 to 0.08 to reflect the non-zero but low-probability petition risk, with a plausible range capped at 0.12 given uncertainties around potential late petitions and legal developments.

causal-factors.name: Petition threat to overturn Lamag result

causal-factors.name: Historical rarity of overturns in Malaysian election petitions
causal-factors.rationale: Malaysia has a history of election petitions rarely overturning results, with only a small number having led to voided outcomes. ([thestar.com.my](https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2026/01/08/pis-will-not-contest-kinabatangan-lamag-by-elections?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Lamag by-election margin and BN majority
causal-factors.rationale: BN won Lamag by a wide margin (7,269 to 1,588, about 82% to 18%), which reduces the likelihood of reversal unless substantial irregularities are proven. ([sinardaily.my](https://www.sinardaily.my/ampArticle/733335?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Incumbent BN advantage and Sabah unity government backing
causal-factors.rationale: The Lamag by-election occurred under a Sabah unity government with strong BN backing, a context associated with political stability and lower overturn risk. ([thestar.com.my](https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2026/01/25/kinabatangan-lamag-wins-testament-to-unity-govts-strength-says-gagasan-veep?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: No confirmed petition reported as of May 1, 2026
causal-factors.rationale: As of early May 2026 there are no widely reported petitions overturning Lamag, which modestly lowers the short-term risk. ([malaysia.news.yahoo.com](https://malaysia.news.yahoo.com/bn-retains-lamag-seat-mohd-144419962.html/?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Election petitions against Lamag result
causal-factors.rationale: The petition route exists and Sabah has a history of election petitions; while no Lamag petition had been reported by March 1, 2026, a petition could overturn the result. ([malaymail.com](https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2026/01/24/bn-retains-lamag-seat-mohd-ismail-wins-with-majority-of-5681-kinabatangan-result-still-unofficial/206706?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Strong BN majority in Lamag by-election
causal-factors.rationale: BN won Lamag by 5,681 votes, indicating durable support that lowers the likelihood of reversal. ([sinardaily.my](https://www.sinardaily.my/article/733335/focus/national/bn-retains-lamag-seat-ismail-wins-with-majority-of-5681?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Historical precedents of court overturns in Malaysia
causal-factors.rationale: There are rare precedents where election results were nullified by courts (e.g., Cameron Highlands 2018, Kimanis 2019), establishing a non-zero overturn risk. ([theborneopost.com](https://www.theborneopost.com/2025/12/31/third-election-petition-filed/?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Past narrow margin in the preceding Lamag general election
causal-factors.rationale: The 2025 Lamag general election was decided by only 153 votes, suggesting fragility that petitions could exploit even if the by-election margin is larger. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Lamag_by-election?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Sabah election-petition environment could trigger more by-elections
causal-factors.rationale: Warisan and others have noted that election petitions could trigger additional by-elections, reflecting an active petition environment in Sabah. ([malaysiakini.com](https://www.malaysiakini.com/news/766473/?utm_source=openai))

synthesis: The baseline 4% ensemble suggests a small overturn risk. Considering a credible petition path in Sabah and a litigious environment, I modestly scale the probability upward to about 8%, while acknowledging the large margin and historical rarity of reversals keep the risk well below 15%.
